record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: Let K be a compact Hausdorff space. Does there exist a totally disconnected compact Hausdorff space K₀ such that the Banach spaces C(K) and C(K₀) are isomorphic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For every compact Hausdorff space $K$, let $C(K)$ denote the Banach space of all continuous real-valued (equivalently, complex-valued) functions on $K$, equipped with the supremum norm. A compact Hausdorff space is said to be totally disconnected if its only connected subsets are singletons. Two Banach spaces are isomorphic if there exists a linear bijection between them which is bounded with bounded inverse.

Question: Is it true that for every compact Hausdorff space $K$ there exists a totally disconnected compact Hausdorff space $K_0$ such that $C(K)$ is isomorphic to $C(K_0)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has a consistently negative answer: under the Continuum Hypothesis, P. Koszmider constructed a compact Hausdorff space $K$ such that $C(K)$ is not isomorphic to $C(L)$ for any totally disconnected compact Hausdorff space $L$. Positive results are known for restricted classes (e.g., compact metric spaces by Milutin, compact abelian groups and products of compact metric spaces by Pełczyński), but in full generality the answer is no (consistently).

status_evidence.title: Pełczyński – an overview (ScienceDirect Topics)
status_evidence.snippet: Assuming CH, P. Koszmider has shown that there is a compact space K, such that for any totally disconnected space L, C(K) is not isomorphic to C(L). Pełczyński proved positive results for compact abelian groups and for products of metrizable compact spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Under CH there exists a compact Hausdorff K such that C(K) is not isomorphic to C(L) for any totally disconnected compact Hausdorff L, giving a consistent negative answer.
